To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of vWF and ET-1 are significantly increased in EOPE and ecalampsia and a negative correlation was found between vWF levels and pregnancy outcome; GA & BW.

the circulating levels of markers for endothelial dysfunction are significantly elevated in EOPE and in eclampsia compared with CPW, GH, LOPE and that there is a negative correlation between vWF levels and GA, BW.

the circulating levels of markers for endothelial dysfunction: PMPs, ET-1 and vWF were found to be increased in hypertensive disorders and the levels were significantly higher in early onset preeclampia and eclampsia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a spectrum of markers of endothelium dysfunction in hypertensive disorders and their association with poor birth outcomes in a South Indian Population.
a pilot study of endothelial dysfunction and the associated pregnancy complications in hypertensive disorders.
a novel aspect of the pathophysiology of hypertensive disorders during pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the markers of endothelial activation are increased in EOPE and in eclampsia and are associated with poor pregnancy outcome.
endothelial dysfunction is the underlying mechanism of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy and it is more severe in early onset preeclampia and eclampsia.
the markers of endothelial activation are elevated in EOPE and eclempsia compared to CPWs, GH and LOEP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a generalized endothelial dysfunction in EOPE and in eclampsia, and this may be a reason for poor pregnancy outcome in the form of lower GA and BW.
endothelial dysfunction and the associated poor pregnancy outcome are more pronounced in EOPE and early onset E.
the markers of endothelial dysfunctions: vWF, ET-1 and PMPs are elevated in hypertensive disorders and are associated with poor pregnancy outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the markers of endothelial function can help in predicting the severity of the disease and also the outcome of the pregnancy.
the circulating levels of vWF can be used as a biomarker for early diagnosis and prediction of the severity of hypertensive disorders.
the circulating levels of vWF and ET-1 can be used as biomarkers for early detection of hypertensive disorders and poor pregnancy outcome.
